newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to decline 2nd tranche of IMF loan - Matos.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to decline 2nd tranche of IMF loan - Matos.

text.p: Venezuela's Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar confirmed Wednesday that Venezuela would decline a second installment of a $1.4 billion standby loan from the International Monetary Fund.
"At this moment Venezuela is not going to use it (the second tranche) and will leave it there," Matos told a news conference in Caracas by telephone from Washington.

He insisted that Venezuela would continue the economic reform program it launched with the IMF's backing in mid-April with or without the loan. Venezuela received a first installment of around $500 million from the IMF in July and was due to receive a second tranche of about $500 million in late October pending a positive appraisal by an IMF team that arrives in Caracas on October 19, Matos said.
The IMF supported Venezuela's decision to forego the loan, which was due to the recent rapid growth of foreign reserves.
Reserves have rocketed $2.874 billion, or 30 percent, to $12.574 billion in the last five months.

"Venezuela is not going to use the second tranche because international reserves are in totally satisfactory levels to the extent that we have had an appreciation of the currency without intervention of the Venezuelan Central Bank," Matos said.
The Venezuelan bolivar had firmed to 466.00/467.25 per dollar by mid morning Wednesday compared with 469.00/470.00 at Tuesday's close.
